game.over_told: The game's boxes were told over the field radio that it is over.
game.over_not_told: The boxes could not be told over the radio ({why}): restart each box, or join it to the next game with a card.

controller.promote_hint: Promote a standby controller when the main one stops answering (manual failover, ADR-P2-8).

score.timeline: Score over time since the console opened

events.medic_heal: {player} was healed (heals left in the kit: {remaining}; heals in this game: {used})
events.hacking_solved_code: {team} solved a hacking terminal ({puzzle}) and got the code {code}
events.scenario_objective_revealed_all: The objective {objective} is revealed to every team
events.scenario_objective_revealed_all_hidden: An objective is revealed to every team

nodes.title: Boxes
nodes.none: No boxes in this game yet.
nodes.name: Name
nodes.conflict: Two boxes share node {node}: one join was used on two boxes, and they use the same radio nonces. Take one of them out of the game and join it again with a new join (Join).

field.title: Field
field.bad_type: The field image must be PNG, JPEG or WebP.
field.no_image: No field image: the boxes are shown on a grid.
field.drag_hint: Drag the boxes to where they are on the field.

georef.title: Map position (ATAK)
georef.intro: Give two opposite corners of the field image their latitude and longitude, copied from a map app as "latitude, longitude". The image must have north at the top. The ATAK feed uses them to put the boxes on a map; a new image clears them.
georef.none: The image has no map position yet: the ATAK feed sends no boxes.
georef.points: Set with {n} control points through the API (they agree to {residual} m). Saving two corners replaces them.
georef.privacy: The ATAK feed sends the boxes and the extraction zone to anyone on the field Wi-Fi; player positions never go there, only to the staff devices set in controller.toml.
georef.atak_on: ATAK feed: on, {markers} markers on the map, {sent} messages sent.

levels.hint_off: Tick it if the field is a building with several floors: each floor has its own plan and each box sits on its floor.
levels.hint_on: Each level has its own floor plan. Choose the level with the tabs above the plan. For a basement, give a level that name.
levels.name: Name of level {n}
levels.no_image: {name} has no plan yet: the boxes on this level are shown on a grid.
levels.confirm_off: Turn levels off? Only the plan of {ground} stays in use, as the field image, and every box shows on it. The other plans, the names and each box's level are kept and come back if you turn levels on again.
levels.confirm_fewer: With fewer levels, the plans of {names} are deleted and the boxes on those levels move to {ground}. Go on?
levels.georef_shared: This level uses the map position of {ground}: the plans are drawn to the same scale and frame. Give it two corners only if its plan differs.

join.title: Join boxes and controllers
join.intro: Make the join data for a box (NFC card or serial console) or for a standby controller.
join.warning: Careful: this code and the card carry the game key. Show them only to the people setting up the field.
join.qr_label: QR code with the join data
join.copy_failed: Could not copy: select the text and copy it by hand.
join.nfc_hint: Bytes to write to the card's memory from page 4 (NDEF message).
join.no_game: No game is running on this controller.
join.standby_intro: Paste the text the main controller made for a standby controller. Both controllers must share the same field join key.
join.standby_done: This controller is now on standby in game {game}.
join.gm_only: Only the organisers can make join data.
join.standby_cannot_issue: A standby controller does not make join data; use the controller in charge.
join.scenario_hint: The scenario finds its boxes by these names: {done} of {n} have a box.

scoreboard.title: Scoreboard
scoreboard.token_needed: Open the scoreboard with the read code in its address: …/scoreboard.html#token=CODE

radio.title: Field radio channel
radio.not_chosen: not chosen yet: the recommended one applies
radio.low_power_warning: This channel allows only 25 mW and about a tenth of the recommended channel's airtime: less range, and with many boxes their transmissions may run out of allowed time.
radio.first_setup: Before the first game, choose the field's radio channel. Until then it is {channel} MHz, the recommended one.
radio.why_1: It is the centre of 869.4–869.65 MHz, the only part of the European 868 MHz band where a device may transmit up to 10% of the time at up to 500 mW (ERP). Everywhere else in 868–870 MHz the rules allow 1% of the time (0.1% on 868.7–869.2 MHz) at 25 mW: about a tenth of the airtime, and much less range.
radio.why_2: 868.1, 868.3 and 868.5 MHz are the channels every LoRaWAN device in Europe starts on, so they are often busy.
radio.why_3: The recommended channel is shared: LoRaWAN gateways send some of their replies on 869.525 MHz, and Meshtastic's European default is the same frequency. Their packets are not mistaken for the game's (the game's are encrypted and use another sync word), but every transmission nearby uses the same airtime. If such users are near the field, a scan shows whether another channel is quieter.
radio.locked_game: A game is live: end it to change the channel.
radio.default_hint: {channel} MHz: the most airtime and power European rules allow (see above).
radio.scan_hint: The USB modem listens to each candidate channel, about {seconds} s in all, without transmitting, and lists them quietest first. Nothing changes until you accept.

unavailable.no_modem: No USB modem is configured, so there is no radio to measure the noise with. The channel stays as it is.
unavailable.modem_down: The USB modem is not connected; the scan needs it.
unavailable.no_radio: The USB modem has no radio chip, so it cannot measure the noise.
unavailable.old_firmware: The USB modem's firmware cannot measure noise: update it.

suggest.quiet_full_power: Suggested: {channel} MHz, the quietest full-power channel ({limits}).
suggest.quietest: Suggested: {channel} MHz, the quietest channel ({limits}). The 500 mW channels were noisier.
suggest.quietest_but_noisy: Every channel is noisy. The least noisy is {channel} MHz ({limits}).

radio.results_caption: Quietest first. Quiet: 90% of the readings at {threshold} dBm or lower, and little LoRa activity.
radio.random_hint: Draws one of the candidate channels. It will usually be a 1%, 25 mW channel; only 869.475, 869.525 and 869.575 MHz give 10% and 500 mW.
radio.low_airtime_warning: 0.1% of the time: about 3.6 s of transmission per hour for each device, too little for a game.
radio.read_only: Only the organisers can change the channel.

checkin.title: Field check-in
checkin.intro: Players scan the field's poster with the app, check in and declare the replicas they will use in this game. Names are shown only here and in the marshals' view.
checkin.empty: Nobody has checked in to this game yet.
checkin.name: Name
checkin.manual_hint: For players without the app: the controller makes their id, which can be written to a player tag.
checkin.valid_day: A pass counts for the rest of the day at this field.
checkin.valid_game: Every game asks for a new chronograph.
checkin.unregistered: not registered at the field yet
checkin.confirm_staff: by the GM or a marshal
checkin.federation_note: The federation number is never verified automatically: “required” only stops the form being sent without it. Tick “card seen” once you have seen the card.
checkin.poster_intro: Print it once and put it up in the check-in area: it serves every game at the field. It holds no key and no password.
checkin.poster_urls: The controller's https addresses (one per line)
checkin.no_game: No game is live: create one to open check-in. The poster can be printed now.
checkin.ticket_hint: Scan or paste the code of a registered player's printed ticket (atalaia:ticket:…).
checkin.schedule_intro: The site server's published games of the coming days. A game made from one takes its title, mode and teams; its registered players then appear here as expected.

problems.https_off: HTTPS is off on the controller ([api] tls_port = 0): the poster needs the field's certificate.
problems.no_address: The poster has no https address for the controller: set the addresses below, [checkin] urls or [api] tls_names.
problems.too_long: The poster does not fit in a QR code: fewer or shorter addresses, or a shorter field name.

checkin.schedule_none: No scheduled games pulled from the site server yet.

poster.title: Check-in poster
poster.login: Open the console with the GM token first.
poster.no_text: The poster cannot be made yet.
poster.qr_label: QR code for checking in at the field
poster.intro: Print this page on A4. The code holds no secrets: it can stay in plain view.
poster.wifi_label: QR code for the Wi-Fi network
poster.wifi_note: The password is used only to draw the Wi-Fi code: it is neither kept nor sent.

branding.title: Field branding
branding.intro: How players see this field: its name, logo, wallpaper and colour, in the app, on the scoreboard, on the check-in poster and in this console. Anyone on the field's network can see them; they hold no personal data.
branding.field_name_hint: Also printed on the check-in poster.
branding.accent_hint: On the app's main buttons and this console's header.
branding.limits: PNG, JPEG or WebP (no SVG). Logo up to 1 MB and 2048 px a side, wallpaper up to 4 MB and 4096 px a side. Metadata such as the camera or where a photo was taken is removed.
branding.rights: Upload only images you have the right to use (your field's or club's own, or with the owner's permission): you are responsible for them.
branding.bad_type: The image must be PNG, JPEG or WebP.
branding.read_only: Only the GM can change the field's branding.

teams.title: Saved teams
teams.intro: Teams that come back: a name and a crest to pick when you create a game. The colour stays the team's colour on the boxes and buttons.
teams.name: Team name
teams.crest_limits: PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 512 KB and 1024 px a side.
teams.for_game_hint: Optional: a name and a crest for each team colour, shown to players, on the scoreboard and on Android props. The boxes keep showing the colour.

scenario.title: Scenario editor
scenario.intro: A scenario is a YAML manifest: the boxes the GM names, and the objectives (capture, code, tags, bomb, escort, defend, survive). The controller checks it as you type; once installed, create a game of it with Objectives in the Game tab.
scenario.ok: No problems: the generated field.lua loads in the core.
scenario.ok_no_core: No problems in the manifest (the core is not loaded on this controller).
scenario.nodes_hint: In the Join tab, give each of these names to a box.
scenario.player_node: a player whose check-in role is {role}
scenario.name: Name
scenario.game_hint: A game of a scenario: in the Game tab, pick the scenario and tick Objectives.
scenario.read_only: The read-only code checks only: installing is the GM's.

firmware.title: Firmware updates
firmware.hint: Upload a signed release (the image and its .release.json), then update the boxes before the game starts. Each box checks the signature again with its own keys and installs over the field Wi-Fi; if the new firmware does not start properly, the box goes back to the previous one.
firmware.no_keys: No release key is configured on this controller ([firmware] release_keys): no release is accepted.
firmware.no_https: This controller does not serve HTTPS: boxes download updates only over HTTPS, checked against the field's certificate.
firmware.not_ready: Updates go out only while the live game has not started: create a game, join the boxes and update them before you start it.
firmware.bad_release_file: The .release.json file could not be read.
firmware.send_again_hint: The box has not answered yet: send the update again now (a box already updating ignores it)
firmware.cancel: Stop waiting for the updates on their way

reasons.no_key: no release key in the box's firmware
reasons.no_link: the box's join has no field certificate or address
reasons.no_wifi: no field Wi-Fi on the box
reasons.unreachable: the box could not reach the controller
reasons.bad_signature: the signature did not verify on the box
reasons.bad_hash: the image was not the signed one
reasons.self_test: the new firmware failed its self-test

results.in_progress: an update is already on its way

adopt.title: Adopt boxes
adopt.intro: A new box is adopted once by this field: it then holds the field join key and takes this field's join cards. A box adopted by another field (or to this field's old key) moves only with its admin PIN.
adopt.previous: The field join key was rotated; boxes still on the old key ({field}) need their admin PIN to be adopted again.
adopt.gm_only: Only the organisers can adopt boxes.
adopt.usb_intro: Plug the new box into this controller by USB and look for it. Check its name and MAC (the box shows them on its serial console; the MAC is also on its USB port's serial number) before you adopt it.
adopt.usb_off: USB adoption is off on this controller ([adopt] usb = false).
adopt.none: No box found. Check the cable (a data cable, not only power) and that the box is switched on.
adopt.busy: a game is joined: end it first
adopt.locked: too many wrong PINs: wait {min} min (a restart does not shorten it)
adopt.confirm_hint: The controller checks it is still that box before it writes the key.
adopt.pin_hint: This box belongs to another field (or to this field's old key): its admin PIN is needed. After five wrong PINs in a row each try waits 1, 2, 4… up to 60 minutes, also after the box restarts.

state.previous_key: adopted to this field's old key ({field})

result.same: Box {name} ({mac}) was already adopted by this field.
result.need_pin: Box {name} belongs to another field: type its admin PIN.
result.locked: Box {name}: too many wrong PINs; try again when the box says so (up to 60 minutes).
result.no_pin: Box {name} belongs to another field and has no admin PIN: set one on the box's USB console ("@admin-pin").
result.busy: Box {name} has a game joined: end the game first.
result.bad_card: A damaged field card was tapped.
result.store_failed: Box {name} could not store the key.
result.channel_changed: the radio left the pairing channel during {name}'s run

adopt.card_intro: Write these bytes on an NTAG215 or NTAG216 card, as a join card, and tap it once on each new box. A box adopted by another field asks for its admin PIN on the keypad.
adopt.card_warning: This card is the field's master secret: it holds the field join key. Whoever has it can make join cards for this field's boxes and read the keys of later games sent over the radio. Keep it locked away, never give it to players, and make as few as you need.
adopt.card_hint: Bytes to write to the card's memory from page 4 (NDEF message, type application/vnd.atalaia.field).
adopt.card_lost: A field card lost or copied? Rotate the key on the controller (python3 -m atalaia_controller join-key --rotate), restart it, adopt every box again and destroy the old cards.
adopt.code_intro: An unadopted box shows a 6-digit code when it starts. Look for boxes on the radio, pick it by its name, and type the code it shows: the box gets this field's key over the radio, sealed, without a cable or a card. A wrong code changes the box's code; three wrong ones make it wait a minute.
adopt.code_listen: Look for boxes on the radio
adopt.code_channel: Listening on {mhz} MHz, where new boxes listen, for five minutes.
adopt.code_none: No box is offering itself yet. Check that its screen shows a code ("@pair" or a restart shows a new one).

code_run.sealing: Pairing {name}: the code matched, sending the key…

code_why.wrong_code: the code was not the one the box shows. Read its screen again: a real box now shows a new code; if its code did not change, this entry was not your box.
code_why.no_answer: no answer: out of range, the code no longer on its screen, or another pairing under way with it (radio interference); try again.
code_why.no_done: it did not confirm; look at its screen.
code_why.fingerprint: it holds another key than this field's.
code_why.duty_cycle: the radio's duty cycle is used up for now.
code_why.channel_changed: the radio left 869.525 MHz (the field's channel, a scan or the modem reconnecting); look for boxes again.

adopt.code_duplicate: More than one box offers itself under this name: type the code only into the entry whose id is the one on the box's screen.

invites.title: Boxes for this game
invites.intro: Boxes whose game is over announce themselves over the radio. Tick the ones for this game: the controller sends each one its join over the radio, encrypted with the field's key.
invites.empty: No free box heard yet. A box announces itself up to 20 s after its game ends (its screen says “Ready”), then about once a minute; “Look for boxes” asks them now.
invites.no_radio: The radio modem is not connected: boxes can be neither heard nor invited.
invites.old_modem: The radio modem's firmware does not carry field frames: update it.
invites.manual: Join cards, QR codes and the serial console work as before (Join tab).

reasons.no_mode: the mode is not on the box
reasons.storage: the box could not store it
reasons.radio: the box's radio may not transmit
reasons.ended: it has played that game already

invites.ready: Ready to start: every role has a box ({counts}). You can close this dialog.
invites.waiting: Still waiting for a box for: {roles}. Joined so far: {counts}.
invites.no_roles: This game needs no box to start. You can close this dialog.
invites.start_question: Review the game's other settings first?

box_language.title: Box language
box_language.intro: The language of the box screens: Ready, waiting for the start, neutral zone, armed, game over. A game keeps the language it was created with, and every join (card, QR code, text, radio invite) carries it. Boxes with older firmware stay in English.
box_language.label: Language on the boxes

choices.auto: This console's language when the game is created

box_language.saved: Saved: games created from now on use it.
box_language.read_only: Only the game master changes it.
